title: Arabic Gum suppresses lipid peroxidation, NF-κB mediated inflammation, and reduces P53/PAX8 expression in amikacin-induced nephrotoxicity
content:
by Hamad Al Shahi, Mohammad Ashafaq, Zia Ur Rehman, Mohamed Eltaib Elmobark, Marwa Qadri, Ali Hanbashi, Saeed Alshahrani, Rayan A. Ahmed, Abdulmajeed M. Jali, Ayed A. Alshamrani, Wedad Mawkili, Faroq Kamli, Ali A. Zarban

Objective

Amikacin (AK) is a potent aminoglycoside antibiotic frequently used to treat serious infections. Despite its efficacy, its application is limited because it poses a significant threat to kidney health, including damage to proximal tubular cells. This study characterizes Arabic gum (AG) and investigated the extent and characteristics of AK‑induced nephrotoxicity in mice and the potential reno‑protective effects of AG.

Methods

Mice were separated into four groups, each containing nine mice. The first group served as the control. A single dose of AK (1.2g/kg) was administered to group 2, AK and AG (25 g/kg for 5 days) to group 3, and AG only to group 4. Afterward, the researchers examined serum kidney markers and conducted a histological study, oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptotic pathways, and to determine the protective efficacy of administering AG with AK.

Results

We observed significant changes in serum markers, including high lipid peroxidation (LPO) levels and reduced GSH and antioxidant enzyme activities, in the mice treated with AK. The researchers also noted distorted inflammatory and apoptotic indices in the AK-treated group compared to the control group. The group treated with both AG and AK showed attenuated LPO levels and kidney serum markers, and increased antioxidant levels, including GSH and antioxidant enzyme systems. However, treating the mice in group 3 with AG and AK mitigated the elevated inflammatory levels and apoptosis observed in group 3.

Conclusions

AG acts as a natural therapeutic with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, and a multi-target protective mechanism against AK-induced kidney injury. Understanding the impacts of AG on AK-induced nephrotoxicity will improve patient outcomes for patients treated with AK.
